realism_constraints: No advanced forensic DNA or electronic surveillance technology available
Communication by wireless radio is possible but limited and vulnerable to interference
Travel by ocean liners and seaplanes is common for transatlantic journeys
location: London, England; Dartmoor; aboard the ocean liner Escorial in the North Atlantic and Arctic seas
institution: Scotland Yard; Proud Sons of Ragousa (secret society)
crime_subtype: secret society conspiracy and ship hijacking

cast.name: Betty Carew (Betty Stone)
cast.role_archetype: young woman caught in a sinister plot
cast.private_secret: married to Dr. Laffin under duress
cast.alibi_window: throughout the story, mostly captive or under watch

cast.name: Dr. Joshua Laffin
cast.public_persona: doctor and head of the Twenty-Third Degree of Proud Sons of Ragousa
cast.private_secret: criminal, forger, murderer, secret society leader
cast.alibi_window: varied, but often alone or with accomplices
cast.stakes: control of lottery funds and secret book

cast.name: Clive Lowbridge
cast.alibi_window: varied, but often with Laffin or alone

surface_summary: Betty Carew, an actress and ward of Dr. Laffin, is forced into a humiliating publicity stunt involving a desk store window. Soon after, a series of mysterious events including a murder, abduction, and a ship hijacking unfold, involving secret societies and a struggle for control of a lottery fortune.
accepted_facts: Betty Carew was forced by Dr. Laffin to work in a shop window advertising a desk
Brother John was murdered in the street after investigating the Proud Sons of Ragousa
The ocean liner Escorial was hijacked by a gang including Dr. Laffin and Clive Lowbridge
Inspector Bullott and Bill Holbrook worked together to uncover the conspiracy
inferred_conclusions: Dr. Laffin was the sole mastermind behind the crimes
Clive Lowbridge was innocent and a victim of circumstance
Toby Marsh was merely an informant with no active role in the hijacking
mechanism_description: Dr. Joshua Laffin conspired with Clive Lowbridge and others to seize control of the Proud Sons of Ragousa lottery funds and abduct Betty Carew to secure a secret book containing the society's secrets. They orchestrated a complex plan involving the staged publicity stunt, murder of Brother John, and the hijacking of the ocean liner Escorial to transport the lottery money. The plot was ultimately foiled by Bill Holbrook, Inspector Bullott, and Toby Marsh, who revealed Lowbridge as the true Grand Prior and murderer.
delivery_path: Laffin gains high office in the Twenty-Third Degree of the Proud Sons of Ragousa
Betty Carew is forced into the desk store publicity stunt as the 'Messenger'
Brother John investigates and is murdered by Lowbridge
Laffin and Lowbridge plan and execute the hijacking of the Escorial
Toby Marsh infiltrates the ship and aids the police
Bill Holbrook infiltrates the ship disguised as a steward and takes control of the wireless
Inspector Bullott leads a raid and arrests the conspirators
outcome_result: The conspiracy is exposed, Dr. Laffin is killed by Harvey Hale, Lowbridge is arrested for murder, and the hijacking is foiled with the help of Bill Holbrook, Inspector Bullott, and Toby Marsh.

false_assumption.statement: Dr. Joshua Laffin was the sole mastermind and perpetrator of all crimes.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Laffin is portrayed as the eccentric, manipulative head of the secret society and is involved in many suspicious activities. His behavior and position make him a natural suspect for the mastermind role.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals Clive Lowbridge's true role as the Grand Prior and actual murderer of Brother John, as well as the involvement of other conspirators like Toby Marsh.

supporting_points: He was found in possession of forged deeds and was suspected of poisoning his uncle
He was seen with Laffin and had motive related to inheritance
He was arrested and charged with murder
His suspicious behavior and presence on the ship
false_solution.the_one_flaw: He was manipulated by Laffin and others, and the true mastermind was Laffin until his death; Lowbridge was not acting alone.

red_herrings.description: Bill Holbrook is initially suspected of complicity due to his close involvement and suspicious behavior.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: His presence at key events and aggressive investigation
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: He is a reporter and investigator working to uncover the truth.

red_herrings.description: Captain Harvey Hale is a disgraced sea captain and suspected of criminal activities including the theft of the oil tanker.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: His criminal past and presence on the hijacked ship
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: He was a henchman acting under orders and was ultimately killed by Lowbridge.

closed_circle.rationale: All key players are either members of the Proud Sons of Ragousa, involved in the conspiracy, or investigators trapped on the ship, with no external unknown suspects.

time_anchors: The hijacking voyage of the Escorial
The date of the lottery drawing (twenty-ninth of July)
time_windows: Betty's captivity in the locked room
The period of the hijacking voyage
The time between Brother John's murder and the arrest
access_objects: The locked room in Camden Road
authority_sources: The Grand Prior of the Proud Sons of Ragousa

The presence of the stolen tanker Thomas Inland

discriminating_test.design: Bill Holbrook infiltrates the wireless cabin disguised as a steward and administers a fast-acting drug to incapacitate the guards. He then sends a radio message to the warships to alert them of the hijacking and the ship's position, exposing the conspirators and foiling their plan.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test reveals the identity and control of the conspirators aboard the Escorial and their plan to hijack the ship and escape with the lottery funds.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Successful transmission of the radio message to the warships without detection or interruption by the hijackers.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed descriptions of the characters, their relationships, and suspicious behaviors. Clues such as the secret society hierarchy, the forged deeds, the mysterious message, and the presence of key characters on the ship are all presented. The reader could deduce the conspiracy, the involvement of Laffin and Lowbridge, and the hijacking plan by carefully piecing together the timeline, character motives, and the significance of the Proud Sons of Ragousa.
